title: Balance sheet / statement of financial position
examples: What is the main difference between assets and liabilities?
Do I list everything on the balance sheet?
How do I make sure the balance sheet always balances?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the balance sheet. It shows what a business owns and owes.

draw.text: Balance sheet / statement of financial position

explain.say: Assets are things the business owns that have value. Cash and buildings are common examples.
Liabilities are amounts the business owes to others. Loans from the bank are a clear example.
Equity represents the owners' stake in the business. It is what is left after paying debts.
The basic equation must always balance. Assets must equal liabilities plus equity.
In real life, if you buy a car with a loan, the car is an asset. The loan is a liability.

draw.text: Car Value = Loan Amount + Your Money

faq.q: What is the difference between a balance sheet and a profit and loss account?
faq.a: The balance sheet is a snapshot at one point in time. The profit and loss account shows performance over a period.
asks: Is the balance sheet for a period or a point?
What does the P&L show versus the balance sheet?

faq.q: Do I list cash as an asset or a liability?
faq.a: Cash is always an asset because it is something the business possesses. It increases the business's wealth.
asks: Can cash ever be a liability?
Where does cash fit on the balance sheet?

faq.q: What does 'equity' actually mean for a beginner?
faq.a: Equity is the residual interest in the assets after deducting liabilities. Think of it as the owner's true share.
asks: If I pay off all debts, what is left?

faq.q: Do I need to classify assets into current and non-current?
faq.a: Yes, it is best practice to classify them. Current assets are used within one year.
asks: What is the difference between short-term and long-term assets?
Should inventory be current or non-current?

faq.a: Accounts payable are short-term debts owed to suppliers for goods bought on credit. You must pay these soon.
asks: Who do I owe money to when I have accounts payable?
Is this a long-term or short-term debt?

facts: The balance sheet shows financial position at a specific date.
The fundamental equation is Assets equals Liabilities plus Equity.
Current assets are expected to be converted to cash within one year.
Non-current assets are long-term items like buildings and machinery.

quiz.say: A business buys a delivery van for cash. Where is the van recorded?
quiz.why: The van is something the business owns and will use for a long time, so it is an asset.

wrong.1: This is wrong because liabilities are debts owed to other people.
wrong.2: This is wrong because equity is the owner's stake, not the item itself.
wrong.3: This is wrong because revenue is recorded on an income statement, not the balance sheet.

quiz.say: A business owes money to its supplier for materials received last week. Where is this recorded?
quiz.why: Owing money to suppliers means the business has a debt, which is a liability.

wrong.1: This is wrong because assets are things the business owns, not what it owes.
wrong.2: This is wrong because equity represents the owner's investment, not a payable debt.
wrong.3: This is wrong because income is earned money, not a debt owed to someone else.

quiz.say: If Assets are 1000 and Liabilities are 300, what is the Equity?
quiz.why: Using the formula, 1000 minus 300 equals 700, keeping the balance sheet correct.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you cannot add assets and liabilities together.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you are ignoring the total value of the assets.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you must account for the money owed to the owners.
